questions.skill: Justify that the inscribed triangle is equilateral
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Points A, B, C, D, E, F are marked around a circle with center O by stepping the radius. Prove that triangle ACE is equilateral.
questions.prompt_markup: Points A, B, C, D, E, F are marked around a circle with center O by stepping the radius. Prove that triangle ACE is equilateral.
questions.required_method: Show each central angle between consecutive marks is 60°, so AOC, COE, EOA are each 120°, then use congruent triangles (SAS).
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: each small triangle (O, two consecutive marks) is equilateral, so each central angle is 60°; ∠AOC = ∠COE = ∠EOA = 120°; triangles AOC, COE, EOA are congruent by SAS (radii); so AC = CE = EA.

questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A circle has center O and diameter AD. An arc centered at D with radius DO meets the circle at B and C. Prove that triangle ABC is equilateral.
questions.prompt_markup: A circle has center O and diameter AD. An arc centered at D with radius DO meets the circle at B and C. Prove that triangle ABC is equilateral.
questions.required_method: Show △DOB and △DOC are equilateral, find the central angles, and use SAS (or inscribed angles).
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: DB = DO = OB, so △DOB is equilateral and ∠DOB = 60°; likewise ∠DOC = 60°; so ∠BOC = 120° and ∠AOB = ∠AOC = 180° - 60° = 120°; SAS with radii gives AB = BC = CA.

questions.prompt: Explain why stepping a compass set to the radius around a circle returns exactly to the starting point after six steps.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why stepping a compass set to the radius around a circle returns exactly to the starting point after six steps.
questions.correct_answer: Each step makes a 60° central angle, and 6 × 60° = 360°.
questions.required_method: Use the equilateral triangles formed with the center.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: each chord equals the radius, so the triangle with the center is equilateral (60° at O); six steps fill 360°.

questions.prompt_markup: In the stepped construction, points A, B, C, D, E, F lie on a circle with center O, each 60° from the next. Prove that ∠CAE = 60°.
questions.required_method: Use the inscribed angle theorem (or the isosceles triangles AOC and AOE).
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: arc CE (not containing A) measures 120°, and an inscribed angle is half its arc. Alternative: ∠OAC = ∠OAE = 30° from isosceles triangles with 120° apex.
